overview: Convert findings into commitment. Use evidence‑based storytelling, present collateral and roof damage clearly, educate on consequences, and transition to paperwork with confidence.
learningObjectives: Execute the complete post‑inspection presentation sequence
Build damage narratives using evidence and clear language
Transition smoothly from presentation to claim filing
Handle homeowner questions and objections professionally

sections.title: Post‑Inspection Approach
sections.content: Knock confidently and announce findings: ‘Hey [Name], I have a bunch of photos to show you.’ Request a 5–10 minute setting. Maintain eye contact and use iPad professionally.

sections.title: Building the Legal Case Narrative
sections.content: Overview → Collateral → Legal framework (‘We’re like lawyers building a case’) → Damage categories: house ID, each elevation collateral, roof overview/metals, circled hail hits/slashed wind, granules.

sections.title: Hail & Wind Explanation
sections.content: Hail: circular divots, granule loss, freeze‑thaw expansion causes leaks. Wind: creased/missing shingles, lifting, displacement. Use clear photos and chalk marks.

sections.title: Granule Loss Evidence
sections.content: Show granules in gutters/downspouts — protective system failing, reduces lifespan.

sections.title: Insurance Education
sections.content: Carriers mitigate losses; your role is homeowner advocate and storm expert to ensure a fair shake.

sections.title: Transition to Paperwork
sections.content: ‘I’ll grab my iPad so we can get this started.’ Maintain momentum and begin data capture.

activities.title: Build the Case
activities.description: Create a 2‑minute narrative from a photo set.

data.scenario: Present house ID → collateral → roof overview → hail/wind → granules. What sequence and phrases will you use?

activities.title: Common Responses
activities.description: Role‑play: ‘Doesn’t look like much’, ‘Rates will go up’, ‘Give me a quote’.

agnesContent.title: Presentation Coaching
points: Teach simply; avoid jargon until asked
